source_defaults.notes: Dated pre-primary candidate-authored words, reviewed in their complete answer or authored article. Candidate factual claims are not independently verified.

sources.speaker: Samelys Lopez
sources.identity_notes: The signed article identifies Samelys Lopez with an accented surname as the NY15 June23 congressional candidate. This is the reviewed accent/display-name variant of the canonical registry name.

sources.speaker: Samelys Lopez
sources.identity_notes: The interview identifies Samelys Lopez as the South Bronx NY15 congressional candidate using accented and unaccented forms of the surname. Explicit contextual display-name association, not a new legal-name certification.

statements.quote: First, we need Medicare for All
statements.claim: Supports a government-run single-payer program eliminating copays, premiums, deductibles and other out-of-pocket costs; presents a means-tested public option as insufficient.
Explicitly includes undocumented residents in the proposed Medicare for All coverage.
Proposes public pharmaceutical research, development and manufacturing in addition to single-payer financing.

statements.quote: I will fight for a Homes Guarantee
statements.claim: Supports a Homes Guarantee and Ilhan Omar's Homes for All Act, including twelve million affordable homes.

statements.quote: I am supportive of supervised consumption sites
statements.claim: Supports supervised consumption sites and federal funding for pilots; her claims about health effects are campaign statements, not this study's medical advice.
Includes sex-work decriminalization alongside housing and healthcare measures in her response about support for transgender women of color.

statements.quote: I support a version of single payer
statements.claim: Supports single payer conditioned on organized-labor buy-in, specifically 1199, no net loss of Bronx healthcare funding, and no net loss of Bronx healthcare jobs.

statements.quote: Granting healthcare to all undocumented immigrants
statements.claim: Explicitly supports healthcare for all undocumented immigrants, as well as a citizenship proposal.

Answers yes to the specific question about establishing supervised drug-consumption spaces. Only the affirmative answer is quoted; the publisher question supplies the proposition, not extra candidate-authored words.
Answers yes to a compound question supporting sex-work decriminalization and amending H.R.1865 to exclude those who choose sex work. No broader stance on coercion or trafficking is inferred.

statements.quote: free community colleges for low income New Yorkers
statements.claim: Supports free community college and loan forgiveness for low-income New Yorkers; no unmatched Lopez education comparison is invented.

comparisons.analysis: Lopez gives an affirmative single-payer plan eliminating patient charges and rejects a means-tested public option as sufficient. Torres also supports a version of single payer but explicitly conditions support on labor buy-in and preserving Bronx healthcare jobs and funding. This is a difference in stated conditions, not evidence that Torres opposes single payer.
Both explicitly support healthcare access for undocumented residents. The agreement does not remove their distinct statements about single-payer conditions.
Both support supervised consumption sites. Torres's short affirmative response is scoped to the actual consumption-site question, not every other yes in the questionnaire.
Both support sex-work decriminalization. Lopez discusses a package of measures for transgender women of color; Torres answers a question that also names a proposed H.R.1865 amendment.
